correctness.rationale: All quantified graph distances, Hilbert norms and distortion scaling are explicit. A Gram tensor with factor inner product 1/2 gives exact squared shell distances (16/3)(1-2^-k); its edge and apex images determine expansion sqrt(8/3) and every pair is noncontracted. For arbitrary noncontracting embedding, Hilbert-valued Walsh-Parseval yields R<=t and U<=dt/4, while every two-coordinate flip has squared length >=4. The exact two-flip identity 8(dU-V)/(d(d-1)), Cauchy--Schwarz V>=U^2/t, and monotonic quadratic on [0,dt/4] yield t>=8(d-1)/(3d). These hold for all d>=2, so squeezing proves the limit. Averaging Gram matrices and Fourier decomposition proves exact LP, with degree-zero mass removable because the shell-two constraint enforces nonconstant mass>=1. A 4030-assertion exact rational standalone checker corroborates, not replaces, the proof.

originality.rationale: The object is the unit-edge graph cone over the binary Hamming cube, with all nonadjacent cube-vertex distances truncated to two and an actual apex at distance one. Robertson 2023 analyzes the ordinary Hamming distance, whose least distortion grows with dimension. Vallentin 2005 and Cioaba et al. 2021 analyze distance-regular graphs, whereas the apex degree 2^d differs from the cube degree d+1 for all d>=2. Linial and Magen analyze cubes as cycle products without the universal hub. None of the inspected statements supplies the cone family limit sqrt(8/3) or the two-shell extremal argument. Results from a semantic research record search concern Walsh norms, other cube invariants and a Euclidean vertex-plus-center extension problem, not this metric invariant. Historical priority remains uncertain beyond accessible coverage.

value.rationale: A canonical exponentially growing family Q_d has unrestricted Hamming-metric Hilbert distortion of order sqrt(d). A single natural graph-cone operation changes the shortest-path metric to one with the previously uncomputed sharp limiting distortion sqrt(8/3). The proof identifies the precise first- and second-Hamming-shell Fourier obstruction, supplies matching tensor embeddings and a quantitative uniform rate bound, and an exact finite LP for every d. The exact infinite-family limit is mathematically motivated independently of a downstream theorem. This is not a mere reformulation of the original Hamming-cube result.
